segments: Foot is a lightweight, fast, Wayland-native terminal emulator whose shortcuts are configured in foot.ini. The bindings in this article were checked against the Foot 1.28 manual; custom configuration can override the defaults. Terminal shortcuts and shortcuts inside the shell belong to different layers.

Prompt jumping with Ctrl+Shift+z/x requires shell support. The shell must send the correct OSC 133 prompt markers. Using Fish alone does not guarantee that every prompt function provides the same markers.

Customizable Actions with No Default Binding
The following actions can be assigned custom bindings in foot.ini under [key-bindings], but have no default shortcuts:
Jump to the start of the buffer
Jump to the end of the buffer (latest output)
Pipe command output to an external command
URL mode: copy instead of opening
Match with a regular expression and open
Match with a regular expression and copy
No operation (override an unwanted default binding)

General configuration changes should be read by a new instance; server mode also involves the server's configuration lifecycle. In Foot 1.28, SIGUSR1 / SIGUSR2 switch between dark and light color schemes. They are not general configuration-reload signals. Do not send signals to every Foot process in an attempt to “refresh” it.
